text.arabic_uthmani: قُلْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ هَلْ تَنقِمُونَ مِنَّآ إِلَّآ أَنْ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلُ وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَٰسِقُونَ

words.gloss_range: commanded public saying; not inward supposition
words.root_gloss_range: speech/saying root, locally narrowed to an apocopated imperative that launches quoted address
words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) opens as a clipped imperative: the Prophet is commanded to say the challenge, so the ayah begins as delegated public speech rather than detached narration. It forces hidden resentment into an explicit address the audience must hear, and its terse onset then launches a Surah 5 command-to-address pattern also heard at 5:68 and 5:77.

topics.headline: commanded direct-speech frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as a delegated utterance, so the challenge is commanded speech rather than detached report.
topics.reason: The imperative grammar and quoted-complement attachment support a commanded speech frame from the first word.

topics.headline: public saying selected over inward supposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grievance is forced into public address, while broader inner-supposition senses are not selected here.
topics.reason: Speech semantics survive as outward articulation because the verb governs the following utterance.

topics.headline: clipped command onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the terse command prepare the longer vocative that follows.
topics.reason: The apocopated imperative and short surface make the onset compact.

topics.headline: Surah 5 command-to-address refrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this address as one moment in a Surah 5 sequence of command-to-say confrontations (5:68; 5:77).
topics.reason: The supplied rows give concrete Surah 5 parallels, so the formula can be retained as local context.

words.gloss_range: vocative call particle introducing direct address
words.prose: {{ar:يَٰٓ}} ({{tr:yā}}) turns that command outward into direct summons. The long vocative makes the audience audibly present before the accusation begins.

topics.headline: vocative summons before accusation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audience is summoned face-to-face before the question begins.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following called construct and turns the utterance into direct address.

topics.headline: lengthened call after clipped command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a shift from abrupt command into an extended call.
topics.reason: The written vocative surface and phonetic rows support the sound contrast.

words.gloss_range: scripture-defined people, insiders, or qualified household of a domain
words.root_gloss_range: belonging, household, inhabitants, and qualification, locally tied to the Book construct
words.prose: {{ar:أَهْلَ}} ({{tr:ahla}}) is the called construct head, singular in form but collective in address. Its root range of belonging, household, and qualification survives because the following Book makes the addressees scripture-defined insiders whose claimed competence is being tested; the repeated Surah 5 address pattern includes 5:15, 5:19, 5:68, and 5:77.

topics.headline: construct title binds audience to the Book
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the audience is addressed through a construct title whose identity is completed by the Book.
topics.reason: The accusative munādā construct and genitive complement make the title grammatically central.

topics.headline: belonging and insider range sharpen the title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title suggests belonging, familiarity, and qualification, while the local construct keeps that range tied to scripture.
topics.reason: The root range is valid but locally constrained by the Book complement.

topics.headline: repeated People-of-the-Book address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the named audience as part of a repeated Surah 5 direct-address pattern (5:15; 5:19; 5:68; 5:77).
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete formulaic references and boundary movement from third-person description to direct address.

words.gloss_range: the definite Book as scripture, record, prescription, and unified authority
words.root_gloss_range: writing, recording, prescribing, decreeing, with a live joining image that suits a bound scriptural whole
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكِتَٰبِ}} ({{tr:al-kitābi}}) completes the construct as the definite Book, making scripture the audience’s defining authority. The writing, prescription, decree, and joined-whole pressures enrich the title, while the local genitive grammar keeps it functioning as the scriptural identity frame; that frame feeds Surah 5 arguments about faith, judgment, and revelation, including 5:68.

topics.headline: definite Book completes the identity construct
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grievance is aimed at people defined by a known, unified scriptural authority.
topics.reason: The definite genitive noun completes the construct and gives the address its scriptural frame.

topics.headline: writing, prescription, decree, and joined whole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Book-language carries record, prescription, and joined authority, while local grammar keeps it as the title-completing scripture.
topics.reason: The lexical range is meaningful but should not replace the local genitive noun sense.

topics.headline: Surah 5 scripture network
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this Book-title feeding Surah 5 arguments about faith, judgment, and revelation (5:68).
topics.reason: The supplied rows link the Book root with faith and revelation fields in Surah 5.

words.gloss_range: rhetorical yes-no question restricted by the exception that follows
words.prose: {{ar:هَلْ}} ({{tr:hal}}) turns address into a rhetorical rebuke, not a neutral request for information. With the later exception, it narrows the confrontation so that the addressees’ grievance is exposed as belief itself; the short question and longer exception work as paired acoustic edges, and 5:65 answers the charge by making belief the condition of repair.

topics.headline: question restricts the grievance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question does more than ask; it narrows the accusation to the one cause exposed after the exception.
topics.reason: The interrogative particle plus later exception creates rhetorical restriction.

topics.headline: rebuke posture with local parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the question as rebuke and can compare the Surah 5 conditional contrast at 5:65.
topics.reason: The rows frame the interrogative as confrontational and supply a concrete comparison.

topics.headline: hal-illā acoustic frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the question and exception as paired edges of the challenge.
topics.reason: The phonetic row has a modest but concrete payoff for the local frame.

words.gloss_range: ongoing second-person plural resentment or hostile disapproval, not an explicit revenge stem
words.root_gloss_range: disapproval, finding fault, resentment, and vengeance; locally narrowed to grievance in a rhetorical question
words.prose: {{ar:تَنقِمُونَ}} ({{tr:tanqimūna}}) names the addressed group’s ongoing hostile grievance before its object is revealed. The n-q-m range can reach disapproval and vengeance, but the local Form I imperfect and exception frame narrow it to resentment over faith; form-label and vowel-variant notes do not displace that local reading. The wording escalates prior mockery into active grievance, recalls the role-reversing formula of 7:126, and anticipates Surah 5’s later n-q-m retribution language at 5:95.

topics.headline: resentment waits for its object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb names hostile grievance before the exception reveals what they resent.
topics.reason: The object is delayed into the exception clause, and the Form I imperfect keeps the action as grievance rather than explicit revenge.

topics.headline: second-person plural ongoing agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that responsibility lands on the addressed group as an ongoing second-person act.
topics.reason: The imperfect second-person plural form assigns agency directly to the audience.

topics.headline: disapproval-to-vengeance range narrowed to grievance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the hostile moral reaction in the root range, while local syntax narrows it to resentment of faith.
topics.reason: The broader n-q-m range is real, but no explicit revenge act is selected by this local form.

topics.headline: form label and vowel variant constrained locally
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the local imperfect grievance even though form-label and vowel-surface notes complicate the evidence.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar identifies the local form as Form I imperfect, so variant/form notes are checks rather than new meanings.

topics.headline: grievance formula reversed from 7:126
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grievance formula echoes 7:126 while Surah 5 later turns n-q-m toward divine retribution (5:95).
topics.reason: Concrete inter-ayah rows support the echo without making it govern the local parse.

topics.headline: ridicule becomes grievance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices an escalation from mockery or lack of restraint into active hostile grievance.
topics.reason: Boundary and synthesis rows make the discourse escalation visible.

words.gloss_range: from/us as the affected target of resentment
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَّآ}} ({{tr:minnā}}) makes the speakers the affected target: the resentment is directed at us, not abstract doctrine alone. The same target phrase helps the 7:126 echo feel inverted, the first-person suffix links this target to the later recipients of revelation, and the geminated nasal sound makes the target marker audibly heavy where the grievance lands.

topics.headline: the speakers become the grievance target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the resentment is aimed at us, not abstract doctrine alone.
topics.reason: The preposition plus first-person plural pronoun supplies the affected participant of the grievance verb.

topics.headline: target phrase echoes 7:126
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same target wording pattern reappearing from 7:126 with roles inverted.
topics.reason: The rows provide a concrete Pharaoh-era parallel.

topics.headline: thickened target marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the target marker as audibly heavy at the point the grievance lands.
topics.reason: The phonetic row adds a small local sound payoff.

words.gloss_range: restrictive exception, leaving faith as the exposed cause
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّآ}} ({{tr:illā}}) is the pivot that leaves one cause standing. It makes the grievance self-exposing: what they resent is not an injury but the faith clause that follows.

topics.headline: exception exposes the sole charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah turning from accusation to answer: the only exposed grievance is faith.
topics.reason: The exception particle restricts the question and marks the structural pivot.

topics.headline: restriction chain makes ambiguity productive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the question, exception, and following clause working together to make the resentment look self-incriminating.
topics.reason: The synthesis rows connect restriction with the ayah-level pivot.

words.gloss_range: masdariyya/subordinating link that turns believing into the excepted fact
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:an}}) turns the following believing into the excepted fact. The ayah therefore presents the charge as resentment that we believed, not as resentment over some unnamed offense.

topics.headline: believing becomes the excepted fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the believers are resented for the fact of having believed, not for an unnamed act beyond it.
topics.reason: The masdariyya/subordinating particle turns the faith clause into the excepted content while preserving the agents in the following verb.

words.gloss_range: completed collective faith/trust, not mere generic safety
words.root_gloss_range: safety, security, trust, and belief; Form IV selects committed believing/trusting
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنَّا}} ({{tr:āmannā}}) begins the answer with completed collective faith. The root field of security, trust, and belief thickens the claim, while Form IV and the plural suffix keep the selected sense as committed believing; the repeated first-person suffix audibly binds the believers, and the wording echoes the believers’ speech in 7:126 within a Surah 5 faith-and-revelation thread.

topics.headline: completed collective commitment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer begins with a completed first-person plural commitment.
topics.reason: The Form IV perfect and nā suffix make the faith act completed and collective.

topics.headline: security and trust thicken belief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears belief as trust and security, while Form IV keeps committed faith as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The amn root range survives as semantic pressure, but the local verb selects believing/trusting.

topics.headline: faith formula echoes 7:126 and Surah 5
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees this faith claim tied to God and revelation, with a pointed echo of 7:126.
topics.reason: The rows supply faith-field collocations and a concrete inter-ayah echo.

words.gloss_range: object-marking attachment of faith to its object
words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) attaches faith to its object. The preposition makes belief relational and opens a chain that moves from God to revealed content.

topics.headline: preposition attaches faith to its object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that faith is relational, grammatically attached to its object rather than left vague.
topics.reason: The preposition marks the object of the faith verb and fuses to the divine name.

topics.headline: single preposition opens the belief list
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first object of belief opening into a coordinated list of God and revelation.
topics.reason: The prepositional object precedes and anchors the coordinated revelation clauses.

words.gloss_range: the proper divine name as the first object of belief
words.root_gloss_range: deity/worship and related etymological pressures, locally fixed as the proper divine name
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:allāhi}}) is the proper divine name governed by the preposition and heading the faith list. The fused prepositional phrase makes the attachment audible and grammatical; worship and exaltation pressures can color the name, but the local force is not generic deity language, it is belief in God within a wider Quranic register of believing in God and revelation.

topics.headline: proper divine name anchors belief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the faith list begins with the proper divine name, not a generic deity category.
topics.reason: The proper noun is genitive after the preposition and heads the list.

topics.headline: worship and exaltation pressures kept subordinate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels worship and exaltation in the name’s background, while local grammar fixes the proper name as the object of faith.
topics.reason: The derivational pressures are valid but do not override the proper-name reading.

topics.headline: wider faith-in-God register
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the phrase entering a wider Quranic register of believing in God and revelation.
topics.reason: The rows link the divine name densely with faith and descent language.

words.gloss_range: coordinating link from God to revealed content
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) starts the coordinated expansion from God to revelation. The list does not replace the first object of faith; it joins revealed content to the same confession, uses repeated conjunctions as cadence resets, and ties current and prior revelation into the same faith field with Surah 5 echoes at 5:81 and 5:95.

topics.headline: first coordination expands the faith object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the movement from God to revealed content as a coordinated enumeration, not a separate topic.
topics.reason: The first conjunction links the divine-name object to the first revealed-content clause.

topics.headline: coordination activates revelation links
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coordination tying current and prior revelation into the same faith field, with Surah 5 echoes at 5:81 and 5:95.
topics.reason: The rows give cooccurrence and concrete Surah 5 comparison points.

words.gloss_range: open relative pronoun for current revealed content
words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the first relative slot for revealed content. Its openness lets the clause refer broadly to what was sent down to the believers while preparing a parallel slot for prior revelation.

topics.headline: open relative for current revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the content revealed to the believers is left open and then paired with prior revelation.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun opens the first revealed-content slot and prepares the repeated pattern.

words.gloss_range: sent-down revealed content in passive Form IV perfect
words.root_gloss_range: descent, lodging, and sending down; locally passive perfect for current revelation
words.prose: {{ar:أُنزِلَ}} ({{tr:unzila}}) centers the revealed content in a passive Form IV perfect. The descent and lodging image remains vivid, but the form keeps the focus on what was sent down rather than on a gradual process; an active variant can name agency without displacing the local passive, and the repeated descent vocabulary belongs to Surah 5’s revelation thread.

topics.headline: passive descent centers revealed content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what was sent down is centered as content, while the sender is not named in this verb.
topics.reason: The passive Form IV perfect fills the first relative clause.

topics.headline: descent and lodging image narrowed by form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels revelation as descent arriving to recipients, while Form IV perfect keeps the local act as sent-down content rather than gradual revelation.
topics.reason: The n-z-l range survives, but local form and passive morphology constrain it.

topics.headline: active variant and Surah 5 descent thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the passive wording against a variant that names agency, and within Surah 5’s revelation thread.
topics.reason: Accepted variant pressure and local contextual rows qualify the passive without replacing it.

words.gloss_range: direction and recipient phrase: to us
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَيْنَا}} ({{tr:ilaynā}}) marks revelation as directed to us. The first-person suffix now identifies the speakers not only as the target of resentment but as recipients of revelation.

topics.headline: revelation is directed to us
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that revelation is not abstract descent; it reaches the speaking community as recipients.
topics.reason: The ilā phrase with first-person plural pronoun marks recipient direction after the passive descent verb.

topics.headline: first-person chain shifts roles
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the repeated first-person suffix from being resented to receiving revelation.
topics.reason: The rows preserve the pronoun chain and contrast with other recipient phrases.

words.gloss_range: second coordinating link extending the revelation list
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds a matching revelation clause. Its payoff is additive breadth: faith embraces what came to us and what came before, rather than opposing them.

topics.headline: second coordination widens revelation scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prior revelation is added without displacing current revelation.
topics.reason: The second conjunction coordinates a matching revelation clause and creates the repeated local refrain.

words.gloss_range: second open relative pronoun for prior revealed content
words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:mā}}) repeats the open relative design for prior revelation. The parallel wording makes earlier revelation part of the same faith claim.

topics.headline: open relative for prior revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prior revelation is also left open, mirroring the current-revelation slot.
topics.reason: The second relative pronoun repeats the first structure for earlier revelation.

words.gloss_range: sent-down prior revelation in the same passive Form IV perfect
words.root_gloss_range: descent, lodging, and sending down; repeated passive perfect extends the claim backward
words.prose: {{ar:أُنزِلَ}} ({{tr:unzila}}) repeats the same passive descent verb for prior revelation. That repetition gives current and earlier revelation parallel authority, while the descent image now extends backward through time; the same active-variant pressure remains available, and the boundary movement links the mocked worship scene to the sent-down guidance it embodies.

topics.headline: same passive descent extends backward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that current and prior revelation receive the same sent-down verbal form.
topics.reason: The repeated passive perfect equalizes current and prior revelation within the faith claim.

topics.headline: descent image reaches earlier revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the descent image extended backward through time, while the repeated form keeps authority parallel rather than creating a new revelation mode.
topics.reason: The lexical image and before/book fields survive under the local repeated passive form.

topics.headline: active variant and boundary movement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the second passive against the same active-variant pressure and as part of the move from worship scene to revelation claim.
topics.reason: The rows give variant pressure and local boundary context.

words.gloss_range: temporal source marker before the prior-revelation endpoint
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) shifts the phrase into temporal origin. Unlike the earlier target marker, this preposition points to the source point of earlier revelation.

topics.headline: from marks temporal origin before prior revelation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase turning the revelation clause into chronology.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the temporal endpoint and marks origin in time.

topics.headline: same preposition changes function
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks how the earlier target marker becomes a temporal source marker here.
topics.reason: The rows preserve the contrast between the two min phrases.

words.gloss_range: before, with latent facing/receiving pressure kept subordinate to time
words.root_gloss_range: before/facing/receiving/accepting; locally temporal adverbial with omitted complement
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلُ}} ({{tr:qablu}}) closes the revelation enumeration with before. Its omitted complement keeps the prior-revelation horizon open; facing and receiving pressures from the root can animate earlier revelation as something present to be faced and accepted, but the local sense remains temporal. The compact closing sound marks the turn into the final verdict, and the word joins Surah 5’s before-and-after accountability thread.

topics.headline: before closes the revelation enumeration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the faith list closing with an open horizon of prior revelation.
topics.reason: The temporal adverbial endpoint closes the sequence of God, current revelation, and prior revelation.

topics.headline: omitted complement broadens the before horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the form leaves the prior referent unstated, broadening the earlier-revelation horizon.
topics.reason: The indeclinable ḍamma form reflects an omitted genitive complement.

topics.headline: facing and receiving pressure under temporal sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels prior revelation as something faced and receivable, while local grammar keeps before as the selected temporal meaning.
topics.reason: The q-b-l root field is meaningful but does not turn the word into an acceptance verb.

topics.headline: before joins Surah 5 prior-community thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the prior-revelation phrase entering a Surah 5 before-and-after accountability network.
topics.reason: The rows link the word with descent, book, and prior-community themes.

words.gloss_range: conjunction or circumstantial connector into the final verdict
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) carries the final clause into view while keeping two closures live: the verdict may be coordinated as part of what they resent or heard circumstantially as what exposes them. Either way, it pivots from defense of faith to counter-charge.

topics.headline: coordination or circumstance keeps two closures live
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final verdict can be heard as part of what is resented or as the circumstance exposing the resentment.
topics.reason: The conjunction before the final clause allows both coordination and circumstantial force while keeping the clause connected.

topics.headline: pivot from defense to counter-charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah turning from listing faith to directly judging the addressees.
topics.reason: The second-person chain continues into the final verdict, so the pivot remains confrontational.

words.gloss_range: subordinating emphatic fact-clause particle, with variant pressure toward independence
words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّ}} ({{tr:anna}}) introduces the final emphatic fact-clause and governs the majority phrase. Its doubled nasal pressure suits the firm assertion, while the accepted independent variant shows the closure can remain tied to the grievance or stand as a fresh counter-accusation.

topics.headline: anna subordinates an asserted fact
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the majority verdict is presented as an asserted fact inside the clause.
topics.reason: The particle introduces the noun clause and governs the majority phrase.

topics.headline: anna-inna variant splits the closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how the accepted variant can make the verdict either tied to the grievance or independently emphatic.
topics.reason: The variant changes linkage and emphasis without cancelling the local anna reading.

words.gloss_range: elative majority of the addressed group, not everyone
words.root_gloss_range: abundance and greater portion; locally a second-person majority qualifier
words.prose: {{ar:أَكْثَرَكُمْ}} ({{tr:aktharakum}}) measures the verdict: most of you, not all of you. The elative form and second-person suffix make the accusation precise, grammatical, and internal to the addressed group; numerical majority becomes part of a moral evaluation rather than a neutral statistic, with majority-error echoes at 2:100 and 5:81.

topics.headline: majority qualifier prevents totalization
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verdict indicts most of the addressed group without making it a blanket condemnation of all.
topics.reason: The elative form marks the greater portion and preserves the majority/minority distinction.

topics.headline: second-person majority is the subject of the verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final quantification is internal to the directly addressed audience.
topics.reason: The suffix binds the majority to the vocative group and the accusative phrase is the subject of anna.

topics.headline: majority becomes moral evaluation and echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees majority status sharpen blame rather than validate it, with parallels at 2:100 and 5:81.
topics.reason: The rows connect abundance language with the fisq verdict and concrete recurring formulas.

words.gloss_range: active-participle verdict of boundary-breaking deviance
words.root_gloss_range: exiting or bursting beyond bounds; locally a durable plural moral predicate
words.prose: {{ar:فَٰسِقُونَ}} ({{tr:fāsiqūna}}) lands as the final active-participle verdict, naming a standing state rather than a single act. The root image of bursting or exiting bounds makes the label more than generic disobedience, especially for people defined by the Book; its Surah 5 resonance includes the revelation-judgment verdict at 5:47, the closing counter-charge sets up the next comparative rebuke, and the final plural ending with hard consonantal closure makes the landing audible.

topics.headline: active participle names an enduring state
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word labels the majority by a standing state, not just a single past act.
topics.reason: The nominative masculine plural active participle functions as the predicate of the anna clause.

topics.headline: fisq as bursting beyond bounds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the charge as boundary-breaking, especially sharp for people defined by a Book.
topics.reason: The concrete root-image rows support a vivid moral-boundary reading locally applied to the addressees.

topics.headline: Surah 5 verdict echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verdict echoing Surah 5 language about failed response to revelation, including 5:47.
topics.reason: The rows provide concrete Surah 5 links and cooccurrence with book and majority fields.

topics.headline: final word completes the reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah landing on a counter-charge against the accusers and setting up the next comparative rebuke.
topics.reason: The final predicate is the structural landing after the grievance is exposed.

topics.headline: sound closure contrasts prior ending
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final plural ending and hard consonantal close as part of the ayah’s landing.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows give a concrete final-word sound payoff.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The restrictive exception after the focus verb of objection makes belief in God and received revelation the only stated count against the speakers.
baseline_models.mechanism: The question forces the addressees to expose an inverted valuation: the object of their disapproval is not an injury committed by the speakers but their settled assent to a continuous revelation.

activation_trace.role: Supplies fault-finding and displeasure as the governing relation that the exception interrogates.
Supplies heart-settled assent as the conduct paradoxically treated as blameworthy.
Supplies delivered revelation, present and prior, as the content around which the disputed assent settles.

changed_reading.before: The verse merely asks why the addressees dislike the believers.
changed_reading.after: The verse makes the accusers name settled trust in delivered revelation as their only alleged grievance, thereby putting their standard of blame on trial.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Belief is coordinated with what was sent to the speakers and what was sent earlier.
baseline_models.mechanism: Interior security and assent bind two deliveries across time. The current reception does not cancel the earlier one; the repeated descent and temporal anteriority make faith a continuity-bearing posture.

activation_trace.role: Supplies inward security and reliability as the receiving posture.
Supplies two delivered movements whose shared source joins current and former revelation.
Supplies temporal precedence, turning the second delivery into an earlier link rather than a rival object.

changed_reading.before: Belief is assent to the present message alone.
changed_reading.after: Belief is a secure reception that holds present and prior descents together as one temporally extended trust.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The address names a community by its relation to the Book, but the closing predicate is limited to most of them.
baseline_models.mechanism: Community belonging gathers people around an assembled, obligating corpus; the material image of a ripe date leaving its skin recasts transgression as an exit from that enclosure. The majority quantifier marks extensive breach without erasing the community or making the judgment total.

activation_trace.role: Supplies affiliation and proximity as the social enclosure named by the address.
Supplies assembly of parts as the corpus around which the addressed community is gathered.
Supplies binding determination, making relation to the Book normative rather than merely titular.
Supplies numerical predominance while preserving a remainder outside the predicate.
Supplies a concrete breakout from an enclosing skin as an exploratory model of breached affiliation.

changed_reading.before: People of the Book is a homogeneous label and the closing predicate is a generic denunciation.
changed_reading.after: The address names a community gathered around an obligating corpus, then describes a majority as having broken out of its enclosure while deliberately leaving a non-breaching remainder.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding treatment of religion and prayer as ridicule and aimless activity makes the focus objection an evaluative reversal: purposeful trust is faulted by people who empty worship of serious purpose and whose reason does not restrain that inversion.

activation_trace.role: Anchors the changed model in the focus question about what is being found objectionable.
Supplies derisive valuation, functioning as the opposite standard to the serious assent defended in the focus.
Supplies action without a sound end, showing how a directed religious act is stripped of purpose.
Supplies the absent restraint that would otherwise block the inversion of blame.

structural_cues: 5:57-5:58 immediately precede the focus question and repeat ridicule and play before the judgment that the group does not reason.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ridicule, purposeless activity, and absent rational restraint; I infer that these form the reversed evaluative standard exposed by 5:59. Alternatively, they may identify the disputants without fully causing their objection.

changed_reading.before: The addressees happen to resent the speakers' creed.
changed_reading.after: Their resentment is the next expression of a reversed scale that trivializes directed worship and then treats serious trust as the defect.

context_deltas.mechanism: A spoken claim of belief is carried across an entry and an exit while the concealed interior remains unchanged. The focus claim of belief therefore cannot function as a verbal password; it denotes assent that must penetrate and stabilize the inner person.

activation_trace.role: Anchors belief in inward security and trust rather than in an utterance alone.
Supplies the explicit assent-claim whose adequacy is tested by the surrounding motion and concealment.
Supplies movement into an interior, functioning as a test of what actually accompanies entry.
Supplies movement back outside with the same concealed condition, revealing no inward conversion.

root_profile.summary: Kök, bir şeyi kabul etmeyip kusurlu bulma tutumu ile yapılan kötülüğe cezalandırıcı karşılık verme anlamlarını iki ilişkili dalda düzenler. İkinci dal birinci tutumdan doğabilse de yadsımadan ayrı olarak ceza ve öç sonucunu zorunlu kılar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali yalniz korkunun kalkmasi olarak degil, kalbin yatismasi, guven verme, guvenilirlik, emanet edilen sey, guvenli yer ve dayanilir nitelik alanlariyla birlikte verir. Bu nedenle dalin cercevesi, guvenlik ve guvenilirlik ekseninde hem yalın hem de yapimli ve baglamli kullanislari ayirt ederek korunabilir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalin guven ve korkusuzluk anlamlari ile belirli yapimli ya da soz obegi kullanislari birlikte vardir; tanim bunlari tek bir dar kaliba indirgemez.

concept_map.definition: Korkunun kalkmasiyla kalbin yatismasi, birine guven verilmesi veya bir kimsenin ya da seyin guvenilir kabul edilmesidir. Bu alan guvenli yer, emanet edilen sey, kendisine guvenilen kisi ve dayanilir binek gibi bagimli uygulamalari da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek korkuya karsi guven, ic yatiskinligi ve tehlikeden emin olma halidir.
Guven verme, birini kendi koruma ve teminat alani icine alma olarak kullanilir.
Guvenilirlik, ihanete karsi sadakat, emanet edilen sey ve kendisine guvenilen kisi anlamlarini dogurur.
Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.
Dayanikli ve aksamasindan korkulmayan deve kullanimi, guvenilirlik niteligini canli bir ornege uygular.

يدخل فيه ما يهيأ للنزيل والضيف من طعام وزاد وضيافة، وما يسمى نزلا لأهل الجنة أو النار، والضيف نفسه بلفظ النزيل، والريع والفضل والعطاء إذا شبها بذلك.
يدخل فيه النازلة والنوازل، أي الشدة التي تنزل بالقوم أو بالناس من شدائد الدهر.
يدخل فيه النزال والمنازلة في الحرب، وأن ينزل الفريقان معا للقتال، ولفظ نزال بمعنى انزلوا للحرب.
يدخل فيه قولهم نزل أو نزل القوم إذا أتوا منى، والتعبير عن الحج بالنزول.
يدخل فيه النزالة والنزل كناية عن ماء الرجل وخروجه، وقولهم أنزل ماءه والمرأة تستنزله.
يدخل فيه النزلة بمعنى المرة الواحدة من النزول، وتفسير نزلة أخرى بمرة أخرى، ومنه عند بعضهم النزلة كالزكام بوصفها عارضة.

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlam örgüsü, bağlı bulunulan bir sınırın dışına çıkma tasarımı çevresinde itaat ve buyruktan kopmayı, taze hurmanın kabuğundan çıkışını ve fare için kullanılan küçültmeli kötüleme adını bir araya getirir. Son iki dal, ilk dalın davranışsal anlamını doğrudan paylaşmaz; somut çıkış ve bu çıkışla ya da kötücül sayılmayla açıklanan adlandırma yönünde ayrı uzantılardır.
